_source: Mindustry v159.3 (git 5811844 "Fixed music fade issue"), vanilla core/ only. Evidence: core/src/mindustry/logic/LStatements.java (2637 lines), LExecutor.java (2417 lines), LogicOp.java, LVar.java, LAssembler.java, LParser.java, LUnitControl.java, LLocate.java, RadarTarget.java, RadarSort.java, ConditionOp.java, GlobalVars.java, core/src/mindustry/world/blocks/logic/LogicBlock.java, LogicDisplay.java. No MindustryX sources present in this tree (searched for xlogic/MindustryX/x$ packages and all *.java under any logic/ dir).
_notes: INDEX BASE: every defs/uses entry is an ABSOLUTE 0-based token index in the mlog text line, where index 0 is the first argument after the mnemonic. e.g. 'sensor result block1 @copper' -> 0=result,1=block1,2=@copper; 'ucontrol within x y radius result 0' -> 0=ucontrol-subcommand,1=x,2=y,3=radius,4=result. PARAM ORDER RULE: mlog text order == Java field declaration order of the statement class in LStatements.java. Serialization is generated: LStatement.write(builder) calls LogicIO.write(this, builder) (LStatement.java:283-285) and LStatements.java contains ZERO overrides of write() or read(), so field order is the only thing that can decide the order. Instruction construction (which LVar is the output) comes from each statement's build(LAssembler) override, called at LAssembler.java:38 ('asm.instructions = st.map(l -> l.build(asm))'). DEFS = positions whose LVar is assigned by the instruction body in LExecutor.java (setnum/setobj/setbool/set/setconst). USES = positions whose LVar is dereferenced (num()/numi()/numf()/obj()/bool()/team()/building()/...) during that instruction's run(). 'tokens' marks positions that are parsed as enum/boolean/int tokens (LogicIO reads them by name, never builder.var), i.e. they can NEVER be variables and must be emitted literally. ucontrol: run() evaluates p1,p2,p3 as numbers UNCONDITIONALLY at LExecutor.java:352 (World.unconv(p1.numf()) etc.), so all 21 subcommands literally read indices 1,2,3 even when they ignore them; 'uses' below is that literal set (sound for dead-store analysis) and 'semantic_uses' is the subset that actually affects behaviour. The same unconditional-evaluation situation exists for draw, where the generic branch dereferences x,y,p1..p4 at LExecutor.java:996 and :1013 for every GraphicsType except col(2) and print(11).
index_base: absolute 0-based token index of the argument (index 0 = first arg after the mnemonic)

status.note: LStatements.java:1568-1625 -> ApplyEffectI (LExecutor.java:1739-1750). index0 is a BOOLEAN literal (field clear: the text token is true/false; the docs <apply|clear> wording is UI text), never a variable. The effect slot (index1) CHANGED SHAPE and both builds are measured. v159.3 keeps it as a plain String (only unit/duration go through builder.var, LStatements.java:1618) and LExecutor.java:1743 resolves it with content.statusEffect(effect) = ContentLoader.getByName (ContentLoader.java:228-240), an exact map lookup with no at-sign handling, so only the bare name works. v160.x makes the field an LVar (v160.7 jar: ApplyEffectI.effect descriptor Lmindustry/logic/LVar;) and LParser rewrites a bare KNOWN name to the @status-<name> constant, so a bare known name, @status-<name>, and a variable holding that constant all apply an effect, while @<name>, status-<name> and unknown names are silent no-ops. E-level: out/_bench/_e_status12.py / _e_status13.py, log out/_bench/probe/status-effect-elevel.log, report out/takeover-20261024/20-status-effect-slot-forms.md. index1 stays OUT of uses on purpose: treating it as a variable read makes every correct bare-name line look like an unset variable (3168 INFO hits in a 1421-save sweep), so tools/mlogcheck.py validates the slot directly instead. duration (3) is read only when clearing is false and the effect is not permanent.

and.note: mlog token 'and' is BITWISE and (symbol 'b-and'); the logical and is the token 'land' (symbol 'and'). The text token is the enum constant name, not the display symbol.

ops_meta.text_token: the operator is the enum CONSTANT NAME (LogicOp.name()), e.g. 'land', 'notEqual', 'angleDiff', 'idiv'. The 'symbol' field (LogicOp.java:67) is display-only ('+' for add, 'and' for land, 'b-and' for and, 'flip' for not) and is NOT accepted as text.
ops_meta.aliases_source: Mindustry-Source/core/src/mindustry/logic/LParser.java:11-14 (opNames map, applied to the 'op' statement at LParser.java:74-77)
ops_meta.arg_layout: op <opname> <result> <a> <b>; result is ALWAYS index 1 and is always written with setnum(). Binary operators read a and b (indices 2,3); unary operators read only a (index 2).

builtin_write_notes.@counter: WRITABLE. Created by LAssembler.putVar (LAssembler.java:25) which leaves constant=false, so 'set @counter x' works (SetI checks !to.constant at LExecutor.java:839). This is the documented jump mechanism and 'jump'/'end'/'stop' write it directly.
builtin_write_notes.@ipt: NOT writable with 'set' (created via putConst at LExecutor.java:138, so constant=true), but 'setrate' writes exec.ipt.numval and exec.build.ipt directly (LExecutor.java:2018-2036), bypassing the constant guard.
builtin_write_notes.@unit: NOT writable with 'set'. LAssembler.java:27 does putConst("@unit", null) -> constant=true, so SetI silently drops the assignment. Only 'ubind' writes it, via exec.unit.setconst(...) (LExecutor.java:193,198,202,204), and LogicBlock restores it on load (:428 'executor.unit.objval = oldUnit'). Persistence explicitly special-cases it: LogicBlock.java:915 'if(var != null && (!var.constant || var.name.equals("@unit")))' - that is why @unit shows up in saved-variable lists.

non_mnemonics.#: CommentStatement is declared but NOT registered: '//TODO broken' + '//@RegisterStatement("#")' at LStatements.java:32-33, and its build() returns null (:43-45). So '#' is not an accepted mnemonic in v159.3; a '#' line is just a comment stripped by LParser (LParser.java:98-99).

builtins_source: Mindustry-Source/core/src/mindustry/logic/GlobalVars.java (all entries set var.constant = true at :276-277); per-processor vars created in LAssembler.java:23-30 and LogicBlock.java:396-397,423-425.
builtin_notes: Everything reachable through GlobalVars is constant=true, therefore read-only from mlog: sensor properties (@<LAccess name>), content handles (@copper, @mono, @rain, @serpulo ...), @color<Name>, @<align>, @sfx-<name>, the four count vars (@blockCount/@unitCount/@itemCount/@liquidCount), the time vars, and the privileged @client* and @server/@client flags.
@wait is a special sentinel (GlobalVars.java:77, hidden+privileged) consumed by 'message' (LExecutor.java:1926) - not a normal value.
@queries (the query result array) is created only for privileged processors (LExecutor.java:135) and can never be written by a statement.

docs_crosscheck.summary: 73 of the 86 entries document one of the 53 mnemonics; the remaining 13 are chapter headings. 5 documented argument orders disagree with the source, 1 documents the wrong arity, and 4 document no argument names at all.

disagreements.impact: layer is index 0 in the source, not index 3; the destination 'result' is therefore index 1, not index 0. Docs appear to have followed the in-game UI order (LStatements.java:1366-1381 prints result, then layer, then x, y), not the text order.
every argument after index 0 is shifted relative to the docs.
the WRITTEN argument is index 0 in the source but index 1 in the docs - a def index inversion.
the docs follow the UI order (build() prints 'natural' first at LStatements.java:1742); the text order starts with x.
arity: docs show 7 arguments, the source has 8. 'pan/x' is documented as one merged slot but pan (4), x (5) and y (6) are three separate fields.

disagreements.instruction: read / write / draw / print / printchar / format
disagreements.docs_format: read result = cell1 at 0 / write result to cell1 at 0 / draw (no format string)
disagreements.impact: the docs' 'params' arrays are placeholders ('1','2','3') or missing entirely, so these entries carry no def/use information. The 'format' strings for read/write happen to match the source order; draw has no format at all.
arity and positions agree, but index 0 is a BOOLEAN literal field ('boolean clear', LStatements.java:1569) so the accepted tokens are true/false; 'apply'/'clear' are only the UI button labels.

no ordering error, but the '0' in slot 4 is not a variable: UnitRadarStatement passes null instead of builder.var(radar) (buildFrom() == false), so slot 4 is dead. Both docs and source agree the slot must exist.

confirmed_agree: op (result is the 2nd token, index 1) - the docs' 'op <op> <result> <a> <b>' matches the source exactly.
